In 1987 New Zealand passed a law making the country a nuclear-free zone, banning nuclear-armed and nuclear-powered ships from its ports. It became a pillar of national identity.

The ban grew from protest against French tests at Moruroa. In 1985 French agents sank the Greenpeace ship Rainbow Warrior in Auckland harbour, killing a photographer, which hardened public opinion.

The United States, unable to send its warships, suspended its defence ties with New Zealand under the ANZUS treaty. The Labour government of David Lange held firm. See Bikini tests and Rutherford.
sum: In 1987 New Zealand passed a law making the country a nuclear-free zone, banning nuclear-armed and nuclear-powered ships from its ports. It became a pillar of national identity.
